chapters.title: Inside an AI data centre
chapters.description: Follow a single prompt through the building that answers it. Three things move through here: power in, data through, heat out.

chapters.title: Power arrives first
chapters.description: Grid power lands at 220 kV. An on-site substation and transformers step it down to 415 V. Batteries and diesel generators make sure it never blinks.

chapters.title: The data hall
chapters.description: Racks stand in rows between sealed aisles. Busways carry power overhead, yellow trays carry fibre, and pipes carry coolant straight to every rack.

chapters.title: One rack, 72 GPUs
chapters.description: An NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 rack packs 72 Blackwell GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs into 18 liquid-cooled trays. It draws about 120 kW, roughly ten times a typical server rack.

chapters.title: The compute tray
chapters.description: Each tray holds two GB200 superchips. On each, one Grace CPU feeds two Blackwell GPUs over NVLink-C2C at 900 GB/s, so CPU and GPU memory behave as one.

chapters.title: Blackwell, taken apart
chapters.description: Two reticle-sized dies, built on TSMC 4NP, act as one GPU across a 10 TB/s link. 208 billion transistors, with 192 GB of HBM3e stacked right beside them.

chapters.title: Where the maths happens
chapters.description: Model weights stream out of HBM into cache and on to the streaming multiprocessors. Their tensor cores multiply huge matrices, in precisions as low as FP4.

chapters.title: 72 GPUs, one brain
chapters.description: NVLink switch trays wire every GPU to every other GPU at 1.8 TB/s each. The whole rack behaves like one giant accelerator with 130 TB/s of fabric.

chapters.title: Racks become a cluster
chapters.description: Beyond the rack, every GPU gets its own 400 to 800 Gb/s network port. Leaf and spine switches link thousands of GPUs so they can train or serve one model.

chapters.title: Getting the heat out
chapters.description: Nearly every watt ends up as heat. Coolant enters the trays at about 45 °C and leaves near 65 °C. A CDU hands that heat to facility water, and fans on the roof shed it to outside air.

chapters.title: Power in. Tokens out. Heat away.
chapters.description: A prompt from a phone in Bengaluru crosses fibre, lands on a GPU and streams back as tokens. This whole building exists to keep that loop fast, fed and cool.
